key_insight: EVA-Bench is an end-to-end evaluation framework that both simulates realistic spoken (bot-to-bot) conversations and measures voice-agent quality across the full spectrum of voice-specific failure modes, enabling consistent, scalable benchmarking.
problem_solved: There was no single benchmark that jointly produced realistic simulated audio conversations and measured the full set of voice-specific failure modes (ASR, TTS, latency, turn-taking, task failures), making it hard to evaluate and compare voice agents end-to-end.
method: Orchestrates bot-to-bot audio conversations to generate realistic, multi-turn spoken interactions for simulation and stress-testing.
Implements a comprehensive metrics suite that quantifies voice-specific failures (e.g., recognition/synthesis errors, latency, dialog breakdowns, misinterpretation of user intent).
Provides an end-to-end pipeline for automated evaluation and benchmarking so practitioners can compare systems and surface failure modes systematically.
impact: EVA-Bench gives researchers and engineers a standardized, scalable way to detect, compare, and prioritize voice-agent failures before deployment, accelerating robust system improvement and safer enterprise rollout.
visual_elements: System diagram: pipeline showing bot-to-bot audio orchestration → recording → metric extraction → dashboard.
Failure-mode taxonomy: iconized grid listing ASR, TTS, latency, turn-taking, intent errors with severity examples.
Metric dashboard mockup: comparative bar/heatmap across agents for key voice metrics (WER, latency, task success, dialog recovery).
Simulation example: timeline of a multi-turn bot-to-bot audio interaction highlighting injected errors and detected failures.
paper_title: EVA-Bench: A New End-to-end Framework for Evaluating Voice Agents
paper_authors: Tara Bogavelli, Gabrielle Gauthier Melançon, Katrina Stankiewicz, Oluwanifemi Bamgbose, Fanny Riols
